analysis.title: US Equities Weekly Rundown: Positioning, Flows, and Observations Across the Floor (October 23, 2026)
key_insights: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% on the week to 7,623.68. Drivers were mega-cap tech earnings, an oil-up/rates-down macro backdrop and debate over the durability of the AI infrastructure trade.
US equities were net sold by Prime clients for a 3rd straight week (4 of the last 5). Single-stock long-and-short sales were the largest de-grossing since late July.
Industrials was among the most net sold sectors. Hedge funds sold the group at the fastest pace in more than 6 months (-1.8 SDs on a 1-year basis).
Staples and Real Estate were by far the most net bought sectors, which the desk reads as a defensive posture. Real Estate net buying was the largest in more than 5 years (+2.4 SDs).

The GS floor saw about $20bn of net TMT selling over 2 weeks across all client types and execution channels. That approaches the $23bn sold over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode. Unlike the prior week, there was little rotation into defensives despite gains in Consumer, Utilities and parts of Financials.

US L/S gross leverage rose 2.2 pts to 216.1% (64th percentile on 1 year). Net leverage fell 0.3 pts to 43.4%, the 0th percentile on 5 years. The fundamental long/short ratio fell to 1.503, also the 0th percentile on 5 years.

Managed Money bought Brent call options in October. Of $2.3bn in new gross longs from Oct 6-13, 32% were calls, and buying continued at about $1bn through Oct 20. Brent put-call skew cheapened and dealers look incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Long bond futures have round-tripped the mid-September selloff. December Ultra-Bond futures are up 6% from the 10/7 low, a 40bp move in the implied forward yield on the cheapest-to-deliver bond, versus about 15bp for 2-year yields. The desk links this to the AI basket (-16% from 10/7) and HY CDX spreads (26bp wider).

The desk says elevated rate vol may reduce risk-parity demand for bonds, while bonds' negative correlation with risk assets raises their diversification value for real money. TY put-call skew turned negative this week.

Thursday was a capitulation and de-grossing day driven by AI financing worries and geopolitical escalation. The GS Risk Appetite Indicator had one of its largest drops on record and is at its lowest since April of last year. Friday's volume was -21% vs the 5-day average and -33% vs the 100-day average.

Vol of vol reached its highest level since April (83rd percentile on a 3-year lookback). SPX skew was heavily bid, but desk flows showed less reach for downside protection, which the desk attributes to historically low net exposure.
The NDX-SPX implied vol spread widened to the 98th percentile of the last 5 years. Thursday's widening was the second largest in 5 years.

The GS AI Winners vs AI At Risk pair (GSPUARTI) is down about 13% YTD, and the S&P ex AI index (SPXXAI) has overtaken the S&P 500 on YTD return. The desk calls this a hedge fund deleveraging episode where short-term stops matter more than medium-term value.
The basket desk says momentum factor and AI valuation work support buying the dip, selectively re-entering AI via Power, Hyperscalers, Inference and Cyber.

The basket desk says cyclical headwinds (slowing growth, higher oil, tighter financial conditions, a tightening cycle) remain. It suggests GSXUCYCL as a funding short alongside low-quality expressions.

TMT desk: NDX fell 80bps on the week, the GS TMT Broad AI Basket fell 4.1% and the TMT Mo' Basket fell 7.8%. Earnings weakness in META, LRCX, TTMI and WDC did little to stabilize the group. Clients see the Election, easing macro headwinds or AI datapoints as possible relief. There is growing appetite for non-AI idiosyncratic TMT ideas.

Financials desk: Financials outperformed the market despite weak sentiment. Blackstone's caution on real estate was followed by an 8% rally in the stock against crowded shorts. A barbell of high-quality defensives and cheap value risk-on names outperformed. Life insurance began to leak late in the week on credit spreads and investment portfolios. The lower rate move drove a broad REIT rally.
Industrials and Materials desk: Industrials fell 150bps, Materials rose 125bps as geopolitical tension kept inflation fears and commodity prices elevated. Over 50% of the sector reports next week.

Healthcare desk: earnings updates had mixed guidance, but price action reflected pre-set theme trades more than EPS revisions. MRNA fell 17.5% and MRK fell 1.8% on Thursday after its intismeran data leaked, despite a 0.58 hazard ratio clearing the <0.6 bar, in a sell-the-news reaction.

Next week: S&P implied move through Friday 10/30 is 1.80%. FOMC and BOC decisions are Wednesday, ECB Thursday, BOJ Friday. About 44% of S&P market cap reports (MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC Wednesday; AMZN, INTC Thursday). Brazil election results are due Sunday night.
EWZ 1-month normalized put-call skew is at all-time highs ahead of the Brazil election, yet most desk flow was bullish via EWZ calls, call spreads and GSBZRATE.

earnings_insights: Blackstone reported first among the alternative managers this week, cautioning on real estate. The stock rose 8%, a relief rally against crowded shorts.

Healthcare prints this week: ABT lowered its organic guide and commented on Diabetes/EP pressure. ISRG had light US procedures versus elevated expectations. DHR cut guidance on respiratory. TMO saw some initial picking at LSS with heightened expectations.
CRS fell 25% after a rare miss and guide down. EQPT rose 19% after pre-announcing a beat and raise. ALLE and POOL each rose 15% on better-than-feared reports.

Mega-cap and semi earnings next week: MSFT, GOOG, NOW, KLAC on Wednesday and AMZN, INTC on Thursday. SNDK, STX and SEC/Hynix also report, and ORCL holds an analyst day. About 44% of S&P market cap reports.
Card networks MA and V report next week, with the V guide in particular focus. Senior housing REITs, more alternative managers and insurance brokers also report.

VIX closed at 19.45, down 2.7% on the week and up 30.1% YTD. Vol retraced aggressively early in the week into VIX expiry, then caught a more steadily progressive bid.
US L/S net leverage of 43.4% is at the 0th percentile on 5 years. Gross leverage of 216.1% is at the 64th percentile on 1 year and 91st on 5 years.
Brent 3-month normalized 25 delta put-call skew cheapened and the 4 delta to 50 delta call implied vol ratio rose. Dealers appear incrementally shorter gamma to the upside.

Single-stock net selling was the largest de-grossing since late July. ETF shorts rose 1.7% (+3.6% month over month), led by Credit, Large Cap Equity and Asia-Pac ETFs.
Risk parity models show bond length continuing to unwind.
geopolitical: The US, Iran and Israel are all reportedly planning for a return to military engagement.
Houthis attacked Saudi Arabia and Iran disrupted more shipments through the Persian Gulf, per the desk's account of the Brent options buying.
Geopolitical escalation contributed to Thursday's de-grossing and kept commodity prices and inflation fears elevated.
The Brazil presidential election is due this weekend, with the race tightening since the first round.
